title.quote: Diffusion Models as Constrained Samplers for Optimization with Unknown Constraints
title.justification: Title at the top of the paper.
title.value: Diffusion Models as Constrained Samplers for Optimization with Unknown Constraints

extractions.description: The paper proposes DiffOPT, a framework that reformulates optimization with unknown constraints as sampling from the product of a Boltzmann distribution defined by the objective and a data distribution learned by a diffusion model. For differentiable objectives it uses a guided-diffusion warm-up followed by Langevin dynamics (optionally with Metropolis-Hastings correction); for non-differentiable objectives it uses an iterative importance sampling scheme with the diffusion model as proposal. Experiments cover a synthetic Branin task, six DesignBench offline black-box optimization tasks, and a multi-objective molecule optimization task.

type.quote: Comprehensive experiments on a synthetic dataset, six real-world black-box optimization datasets, and a multi-objective molecule optimization dataset show that our method achieves better or comparable performance with previous state-of-the-art baselines.
type.justification: Primarily empirical with experiments, although it includes theoretical propositions.
